text:
liam_oncall: :rotating_light: Heads up - provisioning failures in us-west1-gpu-pool. Kube-provisioner stalls on attach and nodes fail to come up. Noticed nvme writeback backlog on the ephemeral drives on the hosts.
sam_infra: Can you paste the top I/O stats and dmesg?
liam_oncall: Pasting quick capture from one affected host:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device           r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await  w_await  aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1        120.00  4800.00  4096.00 16384.00    0.00   12.00    2.50    18.20    5.12  99.80
```
And dmesg shows repeated resets: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0: writeback backlog 524288, controller reset
[ 1234.568901] nvme0: io completion timeout, resetting controller
```
```
# kernel: blk-mq throttling and BQL spikes
```
priya_sre: That's consistent with writeback queue saturation. Could be long-lived large writes from batch jobs + ephemeral-cleaner scrub running concurrently.
jacob_graf: We saw increased batch job sharding last night for model-quantized retrain; may have increased random writes. Also firmware on these SKUs is old (nvme fw 1.2.3).
yara_prod: Impact: several canaries timed out and rollback to fallback model triggered. Prod traffic routed to us-east1 but latency increased.
liam_oncall: Quick mitigation options: 1) Pause ephemeral-scrub/defrag cron on affected pools. 2) Drain the worst hosts and move provisioning to us-east1 temporarily. 3) Throttle batch job concurrency for the GPU tenant.
sam_infra: Agreed. I'm going to pause the scrub job for the pool now.
ops-bot: "ephemeral-scrub job" paused by sam_infra at 2026-03-18T16:10:22Z
priya_sre: Also recommend upping writeback_limits and enabling writeback throttling at driver level if supported, or tune dirty_ratio on those hosts to reduce bursts. But that's a kernel tweak and needs patch testing.
jacob_graf: Can we check SMART from the drives? If wear is high, write amplification could be worse and controller behavior more aggressive.
liam_oncall: SMART shows elevated media wear on ~12% of devices in that pool, but not critical. Still, long-term solution probably firmware update + replacing the worst devices.
yara_prod: If we shift capacity cross-region note that cross-region traffic will add ~3-6% cost on bandwidth and extra instance hours, but recovery speed probably worth it for customer SLAs.
sam_infra: I'm initiating a rolling drain of 6 hosts (low-util first) and moving provisioning to us-east1-n1 for the next 30m. Will monitor.
liam_oncall: Thanks. Also adding a short-term autoscaler policy: prefer dedicated-backed nodes in other zones before retrying in same pool.
priya_sre: For the postmortem: capture snapshot of batch job write patterns, scrub schedules, firmware versions, and any recent kernel updates. We should also add a blocker: avoid concurrent large random-write workloads on the same ephemeral pool as gpu-provisioning nodes.
jacob_graf: Can we add a quick smoke test to provisioning that checks nvme util and delays attach if device util > 80%? That would avoid cascading provisioning failures.
yara_prod: +1 on the guard check. Might add ~2s to cold starts but avoids big incidents.
ops-bot: Rolling drain started for us-west1-gpu-pool by sam_infra at 2026-03-18T16:12:05Z
liam_oncall: Monitoring: write latency for hosts under drain dropped from 18ms -> 3ms after scrub paused and drains started. Provisioning success rate recovering to normal.
sam_infra: Post-mitigation actions: schedule firmware upgrades for affected SKU next maintenance window, replace top 10% worn devices, and add job-affinity for heavy-write batch jobs.
priya_sre: I'll open the follow-up ticket with action items and owners. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
liam_oncall: Closing the hot thread for now, will update when FW rollout ETA is set.
